rows.label: Concept
rows.text: Humans (Homo sapiens) are primates in the family Hominidae. Evolution proceeded from bipedal Australopithecus through tool-using Homo habilis and fire-using Homo erectus to Neanderthals and modern Homo sapiens. Key adaptations include bipedalism, brain enlargement, loss of body hair, and the development of language and culture.…

rows.label: Formula
rows.text:
Taxonomic position: Animalia > Chordata > Mammalia > Primates > Hominidae > Homo > Homo sapiens
Evolutionary sequence: Australopithecus → H. habilis → H. erectus → H. neanderthalensis → H. sapiens
Key adaptations: bipedalism, encephalisation, language, culture

rows.label: Conditions
rows.text: Humans are NOT apes; we are hominids (great apes) within the family Hominidae, but a distinct lineage.  ·  Australopithecus was bipedal but had a small brain (~400–500 mL); the brain enlarged later in Homo.

rows.label: Special cases
rows.text: NEB expects the taxonomic position of humans and a clear evolutionary sequence.  ·  Differentiate New World vs Old World monkeys and apes from monkeys (tail).

rows.label: Solved
rows.text: Australopithecus afarensis (Lucy) — bipedal, small brain, ~3.2 Ma.  ·  Homo habilis — "handy man," made Oldowan stone tools, ~2.4 Ma.

rows.label: Limitation
rows.text: Homo habilis (the "handy man") made stone tools; Homo erectus (the "upright man") controlled fire and left Africa.  ·  Neanderthals were NOT primitive; they made tools, buried dead, and had larger brains on average than modern humans.

rows.label: Derivation
rows.text: State taxonomic position of humans  ·  Differentiate New vs Old World monkeys

rows.label: Shortcut
rows.text: Human = H-O-M-O (Homo sapiens) = Mammal + Primate + Hominid.  ·  Apes = no tail; Monkeys = tail (usually).

rows.label: Board question
rows.text: State the position of humans in the animal kingdom.  ·  Differentiate New World and Old World monkeys.

rows.label: Hints
rows.text: State the taxonomic position of humans.  ·  Describe the main features of Australopithecus, H. habilis, and H. erectus.

rows.label: Quick concepts
rows.text: Taxonomic position  ·  Primates  ·  New vs Old World monkeys  ·  Apes

rows.label: Key points
rows.text: Humans: Kingdom Animalia, Phylum Chordata, Class Mammalia, Order Primates, Family Hominidae.  ·  Primates: grasping hands, forward eyes, large brain.  ·  New World (Platyrrhini) vs Old World (Cercopithecinae) monkeys.  ·  Apes (no tail): gorilla, chimpanzee, orangutan, gibbon, humans (hominids).

rows.label: Universal facts
rows.text: Lucy (Australopithecus afarensis, 1974, Ethiopia) is ~3.2 million years old and bipedal.  ·  Humans and chimpanzees share ~98.8% of their DNA.

rows.label: More practice
rows.text: Describe the main features of the three Australopithecus/Homo ancestors.  ·  Explain the sequence of human evolution (bipedalism → tools → brain → language).  ·  What evidence supports human evolution (fossil + molecular)?

rows.label: More hints
rows.text: Explain the sequence of human evolution.  ·  State the evidence for human evolution (fossil + molecular).

rows.label: Extra solved
rows.text: Homo erectus — "upright man," controlled fire, larger brain, left Africa ~1.8 Ma.  ·  Homo neanderthalensis — robust, large brain, cold-adapted, extinct ~40,000 years ago.

rows.label: MCQ drill
rows.text: Humans belong to which family? → B  ·  The "Lucy" fossil belongs to: → B

rows.label: Study notes
rows.text: Position of humans: Kingdom Animalia, Phylum Chordata, Class Mammalia, Order Primates, Family Hominidae, Genus Homo, Species Homo sapiens.  ·  Primates: grasping hands, forward-facing eyes, large brain; include prosimii (lemurs), monkeys, apes, and humans.  ·  New World vs Old World monkeys: New World (Platyrrhini — flat nose, New World); Old World (Cercopithecinae — narrow nose, Old World).

rows.text: Human evolution sequence  ·  Bipedalism  ·  Encephalisation

rows.label: More ideas
rows.text: Fossil evidence  ·  Molecular evidence  ·  Human evolution: bipedalism → tool use → fire → brain enlargement → language.

rows.label: More ideas
rows.text: Fossil evidence: Lucy (Australopithecus), Homo habilis, Homo erectus, Neanderthals.  ·  Molecular: ~98.8% DNA similarity with chimpanzees; divergence ~6–7 Ma.  ·  Bipedalism (upright walking) evolved BEFORE the large brain — a key sequence in human evolution.

rows.label: More ideas
rows.text: Humans and chimpanzees share a common ancestor (~6–7 Ma); we did not evolve "from" chimpanzees.  ·  Homo sapiens — modern human; language, culture, agriculture (~10,000 years ago).  ·  Bipedalism BEFORE encephalisation is a key exam point.

rows.label: More ideas
rows.text: Neanderthals were NOT "primitive"; they had large brains and made tools.  ·  Memorise the taxonomic position of Homo sapiens.  ·  Learn the features of Australopithecus, H. habilis, H. erectus, Neanderthals.
